item.title: Canadiens Could Break Up Detroit’s Larkin Trade With Minnesota
item.description: Danila Yurov has been one of the potential centerpieces in a possible Dylan Larkin trade between the Detroit Red Wings and the Minnesota Wild. The 22-year-old right wing is the young forward Minnesota keeps putting into its offers, and he is the piece those talks keep getting stuck on. Minnesota general manager Bill Guerin could pivot to other options if Detroit keeps playing hardball. Could Yurov be traded to a different team instead? Oct 29, 2026; Saint Paul, Minnesota, USA; New York Islanders forward Casey Cizikas (53) skates with the puck in front of Minnesota Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt (30) and forward Danila Yurov (22) in the third period at Grand Casino Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Montreal Canadiens Could Pivot From Larkin to Danila Yurov The Montreal Canadiens have been interested in trading for Larkin, but Larkin has not cleared them as a destination. TSN Hockey Insider Pierre LeBrun reported in October that Larkin’s approved trade list had grown to 10 teams and still “does not include Montreal at this point.” That leaves the Canadiens hunting for a center they can actually get. Nestor Quixtan of heavy.com thinks that Montreal could potentially go after Yurov in a trade assuming Larkin does not work out for them. Quixtan wrote , “Yurov is another intriguing possibility. The Minnesota Wild forward has reportedly been discussed as a major piece in Minnesota’s pursuit of Larkin. That alone tells us he is viewed as a valuable young asset, even if the Wild would be reluctant to move him for anything other than a significant upgrade.” If Montreal were to acquire Yurov instead of Larkin, it would pull Minnesota’s most talked-about trade chip off the board and foil Detroit’s potential plans to send Larkin to the Wild. Detroit Has Already Balked at a Yurov-Centered Offer Detroit is not sold on Yurov as the headline piece coming back. Daily Faceoff’s Anthony Di Marco reported on Oct. 30 that the Wild “have been dangling center Danila Yurov as the centerpiece of a trade; clearly that hasn’t moved the needle enough for the Red Wings,” and that one assistant general manager told the outlet that Yurov and prospect Charlie Stramel “aren’t going to net the Wild Larkin.” TSN’s Darren Dreger has put interim general manager Shawn Horcoff’s asking price at two “A”-quality prospects, an NHL-ready top-nine forward and a first-round pick. A Dylan Larkin Trade Without Yurov Changes Detroit’s Return If Detroit were to miss out on Yurov, there is a good chance that the Red Wings would either have to take just draft picks from the Wild for Larkin, or they would have to look elsewhere to trade him. There is no doubt that Detroit wants young talent in return for Larkin. Minnesota and Detroit have not agreed to any trade yet for him. Take Yurov out of the conversation and the Wild may not have a package left worth Detroit’s time.

item.title: Michigan paying search firm $250K to find new athletic director
item.description: The University of Michigan is prepared to a pay consultants $250,000 to help find the Ann Arbor-based school's replacement for controversial departing Director of Athletics Warde Manuel . The university tasked TurnkeyZRG, a well-known New Jersey firm, to track down candidates to the lead the school's embattled athletics department, according to contract documents obtained by the Free Press. Ultimately, new school President C. Cybele Raver and the university Board of Regents will pick the next athletic director, but the firm will provide candidates. The agreement, signed in late September, expands on a previous arrangement already in place between the school and consulting firm. The university used the same firm to hire Manuel, former basketball coach Dusty May and in the search for current head football coach Kyle Whittingham. "Candidate confidentiality will be maintained throughout the process, consistent with applicable law and university policy, to ensure a robust candidate pool," reads part of a university statement announcing the commencement of the search. Turnkey received $90,000 at the start of the deal, another $85,000 30 days after the start of the search and is owed a final $75,000 60 days after the start of the search or when a new athletic director is picked, whichever happens first. The search officially started Oct. 1, 2026, two months before Manuel is set to leave. In theory, that means the school might have a new athletic director by the end of the year. Manuel is supposed to help with the transition to a new athletic director. But it's unclear when that new person will be in place, or who might serve as interim athletic director in the meantime. Manuel's departure comes after 11 years the helm, a tenure marked by both national championships and marquee scandals. The school announced he would leave this summer on the same day it released what was described as a summary of findings from a private law firm's $12 million review of the culture of the athletic department. Manuel was the face of the department during a run of unprecedented athletic success, including national championships in both football in January 2024 and men’s basketball earlier this year. However, the investigation by law firm Jenner and Block into the department’s culture and its handling of the firing of former football coach Sherrone Moore found there were gaps in his leadership. item.title: Glasgow 2026 generated £233m - is it a blueprint for future games?
item.description: Josh Kerr was one of the athletes who won gold at Glasgow 2026 [Getty Images] More than a million people attended the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow this summer, and 510 million sports fans watched from around the world, according to a new report. The Glasgow 2026 impact evaluation also found that it generated £233m in economic activity across Scotland, with £158.6m of that in the host city itself. Glasgow stepped in to host a scaled-down version of the event , which featured fewer sports and athletes, after the Australian state of Victoria pulled out due to rising costs in 2024. Organisers promised it would cost the taxpayer nothing and the figures in the new report show they achieved this. Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games Some 2,749 athletes across the 74 Commonwealth nations took part in 10 sports and six para-sports. Over 11 days in July and August, six world records and 152 Commonwealth Games records were set. The overall cost of the games was less than £160m, according to the report. The majority of this money, about £100m, was funded privately by the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) , with the remainder coming from a range of commercial revenues such as ticket sales, broadcast rights, commercial sponsorship and merchandise. And it found that community activity linked to the games reached all of Scotland's local authorities. The games also supported 2,400 full-time equivalent years of employment, with 82 students securing games-time roles. Phil Batty, chief executive of Glasgow 2026, told the BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast : "Glasgow has demonstrated that there is a template for designing an event differently. "I think what is really unique here is that we have used the assets of the place. The amazing venues, the skilled workforce, the communities that must came alive through the course of the 11 days. That's the key here. "So yes, it has been done for less than £160m but there's so many benefits for that." Judo was among the sports featured in the Glasgow Games [Getty Images] A report into the 2014 Commonwealth Games, held in Glasgow 12 years earlier, found that version of the event cost a considerably higher £543m. The Scottish government and Glasgow City Council provided £425m towards the bill, while the rest came from ticket sales, sponsorship and other commercial sources. The report found this year's event cost 85% less to stage than the average of the previous three Games. The 2014 games featured nearly 5,000 athletes who competed in more than 17 sports. Before the 2026 Games, organisers said 500,000 tickets had been made available for sale across the programme, compared with 1.2m for Glasgow 2014. [BBC] Analysis: Glasgow 2026 was never going to have the same look or feel of Glasgow 2014 - it was never meant to. item.title: Tom Brady Blurts Out a Swear Word on Live TV for the Second Time, Fan Jokes It’s Now His ‘Catchphrase’
item.description: NDZ/starmaxinc.com/Newscom/The Mega Agency Tom Brady suffered another slip of the tongue. A month after accidentally using a swear word on live TV , the seven-time Super Bowl champ , 49, blurted out the same one again while playing a trivia game with fellow retired quarterback Drew Brees on the Fox NFL Sunday broadcast on Sunday, November 1. “Drew has the most 300-yard passing games ever. Tom is second. Who’s in third?” host Curt Menefee quizzed them, per a clip posted on X . “Drew Brees,” answered Brady before realizing his mistake and uttering “Oh [expletive]!” The New England Patriots legend quickly made a face and tightly pressed his lips together when he realized his gaffe. X/Ari Meirov “ Peyton Manning is the answer,” Menefee concluded, as the other hosts laughed. “And we let you get away with one, by the way, Tom. item.title: Laporta joins forces with Barcelona mayor in bid to bring 2030 World Cup final to Camp Nou
item.description: Laporta joins forces with Barcelona mayor in bid to bring 2030 World Cup final to Camp Nou Barcelona have ambitious plans for their fully renovated Spotify Camp Nou, with hosting the 2030 World Cup final high on their list of priorities. The Catalan club have already pushed for and secured permission to host the 2029 Champions League final. The ambition to host the World Cup final has now received fresh backing from the city’s political leadership and the Spanish football federation. According to SPORT , Barcelona president Joan Laporta, city mayor Jaume Collboni and Spanish Football Federation president Rafael Louzan have joined forces in pursuit of that common dream. Laporta optimistic about Camp Nou’s World Cup final ambitions Laporta, never one to mince his words, has repeatedly expressed his desire to see Barcelona’s stadium host the 2030 World Cup final. Despite facing strong competition from the Santiago Bernabeu , the Barça president has been quietly confident. “We are optimistic and hope that it happens,” the Barcelona president declared during an event featuring the World Cup trophy at city hall. Joan Laporta wants the 2030 World Cup final at the Spotify Camp Nou. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His ambition is shared by the mayor, Collboni, who has emerged as another major supporter of the candidacy. “We would love July 21, 2030, the day of the World Cup final, to be at Camp Nou. And for Spain’s captain to lift the trophy here again,” the mayor explained. “It is the best stadium and will be the best ground in Europe. We want it to host the World Cup final, and we are working to achieve that dream.” Barcelona face competition from Madrid and Morocco The Spanish federation also welcomed Barcelona’s ambitions, but Louzan stopped short of giving his full backing to the Camp Nou. This is understandable given his position as federation president and the fact that the Santiago Bernabeu is also a realistic option for the event. “Hopefully it happens. There are possibilities,” he acknowledged, while stressing that Spain should host the final. The Camp Nou is shaping up to become one of the best stadiums in Europe. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He insisted on Spain hosting the final because Morocco has emerged as a serious competitor. The African country plans to put forward Grand Stade Hassan II as its preferred venue for the final. The 2030 World Cup is set to be co-hosted by Portugal, Spain and Morocco. However, there appears to be no real pressure from the Portuguese side. Interestingly, Morocco became a co-host of the tournament only because Ukraine could not, due to the prevailing geopolitical conditions. Spain were the original hosts alongside Morocco and are right to demand that the final be hosted there. The Camp Nou will be the biggest and most prestigious stadium in the country once renovations are complete, and it remains to be seen whether Laporta sees his dream realised.

item.title: Who is Joe Fagnano? The Jaguars defense to get crash course on Ravens QB
item.description: Just who in the heck is Joe Fagnano ? The Jacksonville Jaguars defense will be scrambling during a short work week to find out. Barring a fast healing process by Baltimore Ravens second-team quarterback Tyler Huntley, who left Sunday's game vs. the Buffalo Bills with a case of turf toe, and barring any moves to bring in a veteran, the Jaguars will be facing an undrafted rookie in Joe Fagnano on Nov. 5 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore (8:15 p.m., Prime). Fagnano, seeing his first NFL action after Lamar Jackson broke his thumb on the game's first play and Huntley went down in the second quarter, completed 10 of 19 passes for 91 yards, was sacked three times and had two turnovers in the 36-10 loss on Nov. 1 that left the Ravens (4-4) stunned by how quickly their season is now on the edge. Two quarterbacks hurt in the first half is a nightmare scenario. But Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he doesn't buy into bad luck or jinxes. “That would be the self-pity version. I don't really believe in that," he said. "Things happen. It's [about] how you respond. There's no testimony without a test. So, we'll do everything in our power to keep rolling, to keep this thing going, to get it back on the right side, again with whatever that looks like, and whoever that's playing. If it's Joe [Fagnano], we have a lot of belief in Joe.” By the way, it's pronounced "Fin-YAWN-oh." Will the backup QB jinx hit the Jaguars? Minter is now faced with a short week and possibly having to put the ball in the hands of a former UConn star who also played three years at Maine, the alma mater of Jaguars coach Liam Coen . "I thought Joe came in, to his credit, not really getting a lot of reps in preparation, hung in there [and] did some good stuff," Minter said. "It's a short week. It's an opportunity again to stick together, to work together, come together." Since the Jaguars have had a disturbing habit in the past of losing to backup quarterbacks (Davis Mills, Jake Browning, Joe Flacco with two teams, Malik Willis to name a few recent examples), it's doubtful Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will allow the defense to take Fagnano, or Huntley, if he's able to play, lightly. "It's really on us to play our defense better than they play their offense," Jaguars linebacker Foye Oluokun said on Nov. 2 during a virtual news conference with the media, 18 hours after the Jags (5-2) put the finishing touches on a 42-7 victory over the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium and 82 hours before they will play the Ravens. "That's what we're going to focus on this week. I don't want to focus into that backup quarterback stuff. Anybody who's in the NFL is capable enough." item.title: Hornets Have Run Out Of Reasons To Play Sion James
item.description: Charlotte Hornets guard Sion James (4) drives to the basket as Washington Wizards forward Khris Middleton (22) defends in the first half in an NBA Cup game at Capital One Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Charlotte Hornets offense has struggled in a variety of ways without Kon Knueppel and Coby White — dropping their last three games. One of the Hornets’ biggest storylines was Naz Reid getting benched after one half, but eyes have turned to Sion James ‘ play as a starter. James has been forced into a starter role with Knueppel and White sidelined with injuries. The spot starts have gone haywire, and Hornets fans are noticing. The Shooting Slump Has Been Backbreaking To The Hornets’ Offense Frankly, James has been one of the worst shooters in the NBA to start the regular season. He is averaging 3.7 points per game on 22/15/75 shooting splits. Through seven games, James is 9-for-41 from the field and 5-for-33 from three. It’s gone beyond “bad shooting.” Right now, he’s arguably the league’s least efficient scorer. Of every player averaging 15-plus minutes, James ranks dead last in true shooting percentage (30.4). Sion James blows the open reverse layup in the clutch Via: https://t.co/kRD3AN3Nbu pic.twitter.com/EepNPkkMgH — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 1, 2026 Is it truly a slump or pure regression from the second-year guard? It’s not like James is taking bad shots. For example, over 58 percent of his three-point attempts have been wide-open shots. The problem: he’s just not converting them. Last year with the Hornets, James was called upon as a strong 3-and-D player off the bench — and he played well. With more pressure mounting on him as a starter due to injuries to Knueppel and White, his confidence has slowly faded. His shots aren’t falling right now, and Charles Lee needs to make a change to the starting lineup to make it function more efficiently. item.title: How Mercedes can clinch F1 Constructors’ Championship in Brazil
item.description: (Photo by Jayce Illman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kimi Antonelli made history in Sunday’s Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest Drivers’ Champion in the history of the sport. Now he and the rest of Mercedes can turn their eyes to another prize, the Constructors’ Championship. Mercedes had a narrow path to clinching the Constructors’ title last Sunday in Mexico, but now the math is a little easier for them starting with next weekend’s São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos. Here is how the Silver Arrows can clinch the team’s first Constructors’ Championship since 2021 in Brazil. How Mercedes can clinch in São Paulo Thanks to Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico City, and a sixth-place finish from George Russell, Mercedes enters the São Paulo Grand Prix with 630 points, giving the team a commanding 126-point lead over Ferrari with four race weekends remaining, including the upcoming São Paulo Grand Prix: Mercedes: 630 points Ferrari: 504 points Ferrari is the only team with a mathematical chance to catch Mercedes in the standings. Given that each of the remaining races follows the standard Grand Prix format (and does not include an F1 Sprint race) the maximum points available to a team each weekend is 43: 25 points for a win, and 18 points for a second-place finish. That means that to clinch the Constructors’ Championship, Mercedes needs to leave the São Paulo Grand Prix with at least a 129-point lead. After Brazil, only three races will remain, offering a maximum of 129 points. Mercedes has already clinched the “countback” tiebreaker over Ferrari, as the Silver Arrows have won 12 races, compared to two for Ferrari, so even if the Scuderia win every remaining race, Mercedes will have more wins. So if the teams finish level on points, the number of wins serves as the first tiebreaker, and Mercedes has clinched that countback tiebreaker. So how can Mercedes reach that 129-point advantage, and clinch the title in Mexico City? They need to extend the current 126-point lead by just three points. That would push their advantage to 129 points, mathematically eliminating Ferrari from contention. How can they clinch? The first is with a one-two finish in Brazil. If either Antonelli or Russell wins the São Paulo Grand Prix and the other driver finishes second, that would give Mercedes 43 points, moving their season total to 673. Even if Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton combine to finish third and fourth, that would give Ferrari 27 points, bringing their total to 531. And the gap between the two teams would be 142 points, more than enough for Mercedes to clinch. The Silver Arrows can also clinch with a P1-P3 combination. That would give Mercedes 40 points, and move their season total to 670. Then even if Ferrari finish second and fourth, their total would increase to 534 points, a gap of 136 points, more than enough to lock up the title for Mercedes. item.title: Former Munday star L.J. Collier delivers late in Cardinals' win over Cowboys
item.description: Former Munday High School standout L.J. Collier made his presence felt when the Arizona Cardinals needed it most Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys . Collier finished with three tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss, two quarterback hits and two pass breakups as Arizona rallied for a 33-30 overtime victory at AT&T Stadium. His biggest plays came late, too. More: VOTE NOW | Vote for the Week 10 Texoma boys Athlete of the Week More: See the Week 11 Texoma high school football schedule More: UIL volleyball playoffs: Area-round matchups for Texoma teams With Dallas trying to protect its lead in the fourth quarter, Collier knocked down a Dak Prescott pass on third-and-11 with 3:58 remaining. He got to Prescott again less than two minutes later, dropping the Cowboys quarterback for a 6-yard sack — his first of the 2026 season — with 2:09 remaining. Dallas received the ball first in overtime, and Collier knocked down another Prescott pass during a possession that ended with the Cowboys punting. Arizona took advantage, driving into position for Chad Ryland's 42-yard field goal to complete the comeback. It was a strong response from Collier after a costly mistake earlier in the fourth quarter. He was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after the Cardinals appeared to have stopped Dallas on third down. The penalty extended the Cowboys' possession, which eventually produced a field goal and gave Dallas a 27-17 lead. Collier responded by becoming one of Arizona's most disruptive defenders down the stretch. The Cardinals (3-5) trailed 17-3 in the third quarter before rallying behind backup quarterback Gardner Minshew, who threw three touchdown passes after replacing Jacoby Brissett. Arizona tied the game on Minshew's 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds remaining before winning in overtime. Collier, a 2014 Munday graduate, is in his eighth NFL season. The former TCU defensive lineman was selected by Seattle in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft before eventually joining Arizona. item.title: Four-star QB Hunter Fujikawa has committed to Stanford, breaks down why he chose the Cardinal
item.description: Mililani (Hawaii) junior quarterback Hunter Fujikawa has committed to Stanford and broke down why he chose the Cardinal. Stanford picked up their first commitment in the ’28 class and it’s a big one. Fujikawa is one of the top quarterbacks in the country and checks in as the No. 180 player nationally in the Rivals Industry Rankings, an equally weighted average that utilizes all three major recruiting services. Stanford was always on the short list with Fujikawa but we never saw them as the leader in the race. Early on, Oregon and Washington had some buzz and an offer from Michigan made a big impact. He visited UCLA two weeks ago and the Bruins were trending and Ole Miss has been on his short list from the beginning. Everything changed for Fujikawa after he visited the Farm last weekend and saw the Cardinal beat NC State. He said the visit exceeded all expectations and the talented signal caller decided to pull the trigger just a few days later. “Stanford really was the best of both worlds,” Fujikawa said. “It’s more than just football, it’s a chance to get a world-class education as well and the quarterback development is really big there. I’m going to have a chance to learn under some really good coaches and that was big for me. “Having the opportunity to learn from coaches with NFL experience and someone like Andrew Luck, who was the No. 1 overall pick and is still really involved with the program. The coaches really believe in me there and made a point to let me know that. They made it clear that they see me as a big part of the future of the program and I love the vision they have for me and the future of the program.” A special touch on his visit was a FaceTime call with Hawaii prep legend and former Oregon Heisman Trophy winner Marcus Mariota. Mariota is revered by young and old athletes alike from Hawaii, especially quarterbacks. “That was a huge highlight for sure,” Fujikawa said. “Marcus FaceTimed Coach Pritchard while I was meeting with him, and I got to talk to him over the phone and that was really special. “He’s a great quarterback, and I’ve looked up to him since I was young. Hearing him talk about how Coach Pritchard helped him rediscover his love for football made the visit even more meaningful.” Fujikawa said the offense and scheme fit was another huge plus for the Cardinal. “I love the offense,” Fujikawa said. “They broke down clips from my film and put them side by side with clips from their offense to show how similar they are. They run an NFL-style offense, which is exactly what I’m looking for. Just looking at what a great fit it is for me, along with the opportunity to develop as a quarterback, I knew this was the right move for me.”

item.title: Los Angeles Chargers are the latest NFL primetime albatross, unless flex scheduling saves us all
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Few would’ve guessed that we’d get to the month of November and the Los Angeles Chargers would still be sitting with a winless record. Even fewer would’ve believed that knowing that Justin Herbert has started every game. But here we are. The Chargers are 0-7 after their latest loss to the cross-town rival Rams, and any hope for a turnaround seems to be far in the rearview. Instead, questions about Herbert, head coach Jim Harbaugh, and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel are the only things making the Chargers a relevant national storyline. With three Chargers primetime games on the horizon, however, it’ll be incumbent upon the NFL to find some alternatives to the sputtering Bolts, otherwise fans will be subjected to some rather low-stakes football in some of the biggest windows of the season. Unfortunately, the first Chargers primetime game cannot be flexed at all. ESPN’s Monday Night Football in Week 10 features the Chargers and the Baltimore Ravens, a team that is currently down to its third-string quarterback and sitting in last place in the AFC North. But per the NFL’s flex scheduling rules, games cannot be flexed out of Monday Night Football until Week 12, meaning there’s nothing the league or ESPN can do to improve the matchup two weeks from now. Things will get interesting in Week 12 and Week 15, however. The Chargers are scheduled to headline Sunday Night Football in Week 12 against the New England Patriots, a game that can be flexed under the league’s flex scheduling procedures. However, that week is particularly tricky to flex because it is the week of Thanksgiving. The NFL already has six other standalone games scheduled that week: one on Thanksgiving Eve, three on Thanksgiving, one on Black Friday, and one on Monday Night Football . That leaves very few quality games in the Sunday afternoon slate that would be available to flex the Chargers out of primetime. The best options would likely be Saints-Bengals, Falcons-Vikings, or Raiders-Browns; none of which really scream “worthy of primetime placement.” It’ll be interesting to see whether the NFL chooses to utilize a flex here. Week 15 poses another interesting scenario. The Chargers are scheduled to play the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday Night Football . The NFL can flex TNF games after Week 13, but must give a 21-day notice as opposed to the normal six- or 12-day notice the league is usually afforded (depending on which package and how late in the year the flex is happening). Only once in the league’s history has the NFL flexed a Thursday game; in 2024 to swap out Browns-Bengals for Broncos-Chargers. It’s unclear if 49ers-Chargers would meet the threshold for a Thursday flex, considering the 49ers figure to be Super Bowl contenders and that game will likely have playoff implications for them. So despite the Chargers sporting an 0-7 record heading into Week 9, it’s quite possible the team is featured in three primetime slots the remainder of the season.

item.title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Dolphins
item.description: Allow me to be the first to welcome everyone to the best time of the year! 3:30 p.m. sunsets and constant darkness, here we come! It’s wild how I used to actually enjoy the first night of Daylight Savings Time starting, or ending, or whichever one this one is. You’re out at the bars, they’re about to close…and then all of a sudden, you get an extra hour to make bad decisions. But I’ve aged out of all that, alas, so now I’m taking up the mantle of the crotchety middle-aged man who likes to complain about everything. At least I’m not complaining about a Patriots loss, though, as New England took care of business to the tune of a 24-19 victory to move ahead to 5-3, 3-0 in the AFC East . I had absolutely no idea what to expect coming into this game. Sure, the Fins stink, but nothing is as it seems when the Patriots head down to Miami. Compound that with rainy conditions, an oddly-positioned 4:25 slot for a game that certainly didn’t deserve a late window, and an absolutely decimated Patriots team, and this just seemed to have all the makings of a trap game. And for the first half, that’s exactly what seemed to be happening. New England couldn’t move the ball at all, the defense was oddly off, and the whole game just seemed like holiday commercials before Halloween even hits; nobody wants to see that. But something happened in that locker room at halftime, because the Patriots came out and scored on three consecutive drives to open this one up. But I’m getting ahead of myself. I have a few more complaints to lodge before I break this game down in earnest. item.title: 'Just next level': Jayson Tatum shares what has blown him away about Paul George this season
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Jayson Tatum and Paul George have formed quite the partnership since joining forces with the Boston Celtics. On Sunday night, the Celtics secured a 108-97 win against the Orlando Magic on the road, and Tatum showed why he is their star player once again. However, George produced a number of incredible moments, and his fellow forward heaped praise on him after the game. Jayson Tatum says Paul George’s game awareness is ‘just next level’ Paul George has been in the NBA for 17 years now and has played with some big players. The veteran may not have won a championship ring yet, but he is viewed by many as an incredible player, and his performances lately speak for themselves. Against the Magic, George scored 17 points and recorded six rebounds, eight assists, two steals and two blocks during his 33 minutes on the floor. That seems to have impressed Tatum, who heaped praise on him after the game. He said on NBC Sports Boston : “It (the chemistry) is great. We continue to get better. “He hit some unbelievable shots. His awareness on the defensive end and his activity with his hands is just next level. He always has awareness with the ball and deflections. “He makes it easier on the rest of us, even this late in his career.” Tatum had formed a stunning partnership with Jaylen Brown when they were together in Boston, so George had some big shoes to fill. However, so far, he is doing what he is expected to do, which is good news for Celtics fans and their ambitions for the season.
